description: A litigation director must approve the company's response to a discovery demand in a trade-secret lawsuit and set the production safeguards for sensitive records and source code, with input from a discovery associate and a client privacy counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company is defending a trade-secret lawsuit in which the plaintiff has demanded customer-support files, internal spreadsheets, and source-code materials.
shared_context.S2: The current draft response proposes ordinary document production under the court's existing confidentiality order.
shared_context.S3: The plaintiff has indicated that it will challenge any substantial withholding or restriction on access.
shared_context.S4: The court's discovery order requires the company to serve its response to the demand within 10 days.

PF1.text: Marcus completed a review of the custodian export this morning and found exactly 86 spreadsheets containing patient names or diagnoses. The production plan must include de-identified versions of those spreadsheets and redact all patient identifiers because the existing confidentiality order is not a HIPAA-qualified protective order. Because that order is not HIPAA-qualified, a motion for a modified or supplemental protective order must be filed before any of the 86 spreadsheets are produced. This result has not yet been added to the draft response.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed with the client's privacy office after the draft circulated that the client's source-code license agreements prohibit downloadable production of the code. The client requires source-code inspection only in a secure review room by outside counsel, with no employee access or downloads, and Nadia has not yet relayed that confirmation to the litigation team.

acceptance_conditions: The company must file a protective-order motion before responding to the discovery demand.
Exactly 86 patient-related spreadsheets must be produced only as de-identified versions.
All patient identifiers must be redacted.
Source-code access must be limited to outside counsel in a secure review room.
The response must include a patient-data de-identification commitment identifying the 86 spreadsheets and redaction requirement.
The response must include a source-code inspection commitment tied to the client's license agreements.
The response must cite the discovery associate's patient-spreadsheet finding and the client privacy counsel's source-code licensing finding as justifications.

content_checks.C5: 'secure review room' in decisions['source_code_access'] and 'outside counsel' in decisions['source_code_access']
content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Marcus' and '86' in c['detail'] and 'de-ident' in c['detail'] and 'redact' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] == 'Nadia' and 'license' in c['detail'] and 'inspection' in c['detail'] and 'secure review room' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes the response from ordinary production to a protective-order motion before production, an exact count of 86 spreadsheets, de-identified versions, redaction of all patient identifiers, and a commitment naming those 86 spreadsheets.

PF2 changes source-code access from ordinary production to inspection in a secure review room by outside counsel, prohibits downloads, and requires a commitment tying that inspection protocol to the license agreements.
